content.text: {"primary_meaning":"The Holy Spirit—especially the Spirit’s anointing, empowering, and setting apart of a person for divine service—is the symbolic meaning most commonly assigned to oil in Christian teaching.","primary_basis":["1 Samuel 16:13 — David is anointed with oil, and the Spirit of the LORD comes powerfully upon him.","Isaiah 61:1 and Luke 4:18 — the Messiah is described as anointed by the Spirit to carry out his mission.","Acts 10:38 — God anoints Jesus with the Holy Spirit and power.","Zechariah 4:1–14 — the lampstand supplied with oil is commonly connected with God’s Spirit, especially through the declaration, “Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit.”","Exodus 30:22–33; Leviticus 8:10–12 — sacred anointing oil consecrates the tabernacle, priests, and their service."] ,"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Consecration, divine appointment, or authorization for an office such as king, priest, or prophet. This overlaps with Spirit symbolism but can function independently as a sign of being set apart.","basis":["Exodus 29:7; 30:30","Leviticus 8:10–12","1 Samuel 10:1","1 Kings 19:15–16"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Joy, gladness, honor, and festive blessing.","basis":["Psalm 23:5","Psalm 45:7","Isaiah 61:3","Hebrews 1:9"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Healing, soothing care, or medicinal treatment.","basis":["Isaiah 1:6","Mark 6:13","Luke 10:34","James 5:14"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Material provision, prosperity, abundance, or divine blessing, since oil was an important agricultural commodity.","basis":["Deuteronomy 7:13","2 Kings 4:1–7","Joel 2:19,24","Hosea 2:8"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Readiness, vigilance, or persevering faith, particularly in interpretations of the oil carried by the wise virgins.","basis":["Matthew 25:1–13"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Light-bearing testimony or the sustaining divine supply that enables faithful witness.","basis":["Exodus 27:20–21","Leviticus 24:2","Zechariah 4:1–14","Revelation 11:3–4"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"The ordinary practical substance used for grooming, hospitality, burial preparation, food, lamps, or commerce, without a necessary symbolic meaning.","basis":["Matthew 6:17","Luke 7:46","Matthew 25:3–8","Mark 14:8","Revelation 6:6"],"prominence":"common"}],"has_settled_consensus":false,"confidence":"high","notes":"“Oil symbolizes the Holy Spirit” is the dominant shorthand in Christian preaching and typological interpretation. Biblical scholarship generally emphasizes that oil has several context-dependent functions and that no passage establishes a universal one-to-one equation between oil and the Spirit. Thus there is a recognizable primary association, but no settled interpretation applicable to every occurrence."}
